title: Comparative Impact Calculus
description: Essential Criteria: The response explicitly compares competing impacts using at least one of the following dimensions: magnitude, probability, timeframe, or reversibility rather than simply asserting one impact is bigger.

title: Metric Consistency
description: Essential Criteria: The weighing metric applied to the response's own impacts is also applied to the opponent's impacts, using the same standard rather than switching frameworks to favor each side.

title: Framing the Round
description: Important Criteria: The response articulates a reason why the judge should prefer its weighing framework over the opponent's, not just why its impacts are larger within a shared framework.

title: Precedence Argument
description: Optional Criteria: Where impacts are roughly comparable in magnitude, the response provides a principled reason why one type of harm or benefit should take precedence.

title: Unanchored Comparison
description: Pitfall Criteria: Does not compare impacts using vague language like 'more important' or 'outweighs' without specifying the dimension on which the comparison is being made.

title: Double Standard
description: Pitfall Criteria: Does not apply a stricter evidentiary or logical standard to the opponent's impacts than to its own when making comparative claims.
